output.headline: A 20% NVDA position fails governance; the maximum acceptable NVDA weight is about 5%, and the verified proposal holds NVDA at 5% within a diversified, low-moderate-risk mix.

governance.evidence: Final proposal passes all checks: single position max 9.7% (RY.TO incl. ETF look-through); sector max 18.6% vs 35%; crypto 0%; SHORT_HORIZON_VOLATILITY at its 5% limit (exactly at threshold); SHORT_HORIZON_DEFENSIVE 43% vs 30%. The 20% NVDA version is blocked: NVDA single position 20% vs 10%, and short-horizon volatility 20% vs 5% (ev-5f0c1a9d27). The 8% NVDA version is also blocked on short-horizon volatility (8% vs 5%).

details: 20% NVDA does not pass: the short-horizon volatility rule caps NVDA at 5% for a 3-5 year horizon, and 20% would also exceed the 10% single-position limit (ev-5f0c1a9d27).
The 8% version still blocks on the short-horizon volatility rule, so 5% is the highest weight that passes.

Defensive core: XBB.TO (30%) and ZST.TO (13%) are the bond and cash sleeves. XIU.TO (28%) provides broad Canadian equity. JNJ (8%) and RY.TO (7%) add diversification. RY.TO is trimmed to keep its look-through exposure under 10%. FTS.TO is trimmed to 9% to stay under the single-position limit.
Growth is modest by design. The 5% NVDA sleeve is the only high-volatility holding. Raising NVDA further would need either a looser horizon rule or a higher loss tolerance from the investor.
